questiontext:
Express \[{{CT:0}},\] as a sum of partial fractions. [[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
We note that the numerator \[{{CT:1}}\] is cubic and that the denominator \[{{CT:2}}={{CT:3}}\] is quadratic. Dividing {{CT:4}} by {{CT:5}} we obtain a linear term of the form {{CT:6}} and a linear remainder of the form {{CT:7}} and \[{{CT:1}} = ({{CT:3}})({{CT:8}})+{{CT:9}}.\] Expanding out the brackets we find \[{{CT:1}} = {{CT:10}}+{{CT:9}}.\] Matching coefficients we see that \(g={{CT:11}}\) and that \(h={{CT:12}}-{{CT:13}}={{CT:12}}-{{CT:14}}={{CT:15}}\). Also \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle h+m+{{CT:16}}={{CT:15}} + m + {{CT:17}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:18}}\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:19}}+n={{CT:20}}+n&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:21}}\mbox{.} \end{array}\] Therefore \(m={{CT:22}}\) and \(n={{CT:23}}\). The quotient is \({{CT:8}}={{CT:24}}\) and the remainder is \({{CT:9}}={{CT:25}}\). As a sum of partial fractions \[ {{CT:26}}=\frac{A}{{CT:27}}+\frac{B}{{CT:2}}\mbox{.}\]

Multiplying both sides through by {{CT:28}} we find:

\[{{CT:25}}= {{CT:29}} + B\mbox{.}\]

Matching coefficients we see that \(A={{CT:30}}\) and setting \(x={{CT:31}}\) we find that \(B={{CT:32}}\) so

\[ {{CT:26}}=\frac{{CT:30}}{{CT:27}}+\frac{{CT:32}}{{CT:2}}\mbox{.}\] Therefore \[{{CT:0}}={{CT:33}}\mbox{.}\]
